title: Western Sahara, a disputed desert territory, froze North Africa for 50 years — now its fallout spills into Spain
summary: About 50,000 to 60,000 people crossed into Spain's Ceuta exclave in a day in late July 2026, dramatizing a rivalry that has kept the Algeria-Morocco border shut since 1994 and left a regional union without a summit in 30 years — while whether Morocco engineered the surge and whether a new UN push for autonomy will bring talks remain contested.

claims.text: Moroccos 2007 Initiative for Negotiating an Autonomy Statute for the Sahara Region (UN doc S/2007/206, Annex) proposes autonomy under Moroccan sovereignty: devolved legislative, executive and judicial bodies elected by residents, while Rabat retains exclusive powers over national defense, foreign affairs, currency/monetary policy, nationality and supreme judiciary; implementation was said to be subject to approval by 2populations concerned2 in a referendum (paras 8, 27). An expanded 40-page statute presented in Madrid in Feb 2026 (royal advisers Fassi Fihri/Aziman/Himma, FM Bourita) details exclusive vs regional powers, unicameral regional parliament (direct election + tribal appointment), regional high court, fiscal regime, and constitutional entrenchment with irreversibility clause.

claims.text: Human rights conditions in Polisario-administered Tindouf camps (Algeria): HRWs 2013-2014 field research found no pattern of serious abuse but identified concerns d military courts trying civilians (8 of 25 prisoners in 2013), prolonged pre-trial detention without court orders, isolated torture allegations, persistence of slavery-like domestic servitude in small minority despite 2011 legal ban, and one enforced disappearance (El Khalil Ahmed, Algiers 2009); Algeria remains ultimately responsible under international law for rights on its territory despite ceding de facto administration to Polisario; MINURSO has no human rights mandate.
